examples.en: A learner sees a word beginning with a sun letter and still pronounces a full lam, treating every al- prefix the same regardless of the letter that follows it.
A learner reads a prefixed particle and its host as one unfamiliar word instead of separating the small attached piece from the host first.

point_hint.text: Look again at the start of this word: it may begin with a small attached particle.

teach_hint.text: When a word starts with wāw/fāʾ/bāʾ/kāf/lām or al-, that piece is a separate particle with its own meaning; read the host without it, then add the particle's contribution.

examples.en: A learner picks the more familiar reading of an unvoweled word and drops the other possible reading, instead of keeping both until something in the sentence decides.
A learner assumes every letter in an unvoweled word is a root letter without checking whether one of them actually belongs to the pattern instead.

point_hint.text: These letters can be read more than one way; notice that the short vowels are missing.

teach_hint.text: Unvoweled Arabic underdetermines the word: the same letters may be a noun or a verb. Keep the readings side by side and let context or a source decide.

A learner assumes an attached pronoun always matches the word it is written on, rather than the person or thing it actually refers to.

point_hint.text: Look at the ending of this word: it may be an attached pronoun rather than part of the root.

teach_hint.text: An attached pronoun at the end carries 'his/her/their/you/us'; but a lone single letter could also be a radical, so confirm from context before deciding.

examples.en: A learner assigns one fixed English meaning to a small particle without checking whether the surrounding words point to a different job for it here.
A learner treats a multi-function particle as only ever a connector, missing that the same shape can mark a wish, a question, or an exception depending on the sentence.

point_hint.text: This little word has several possible jobs here; look at what surrounds it.

teach_hint.text: A particle like mā or wāw can be negation, a relative, a question, coordination, and more; identify the function from the clause, then gloss it accordingly.
